identity.name: Historiques 222
identity.one_liner: The faithful reissue of Jorg Hysek's 1977 222 — 37mm, hidden Maltese cross on the case flank — in gold first, steel since 2025.

provenance_events.description: Vacheron put the Historiques 222 into stainless steel (ref. 4200H/222A-B934) at $32,000 — the configuration collectors had asked for since the 2022 yellow-gold reissue, and the closest thing to the original 1977 steel 222 the modern catalog offers.

narrative.story: The 222 was Vacheron's 1977 entry in the integrated-bracelet race — designed not by Genta but by a 24-year-old Jorg Hysek for the maison's 222nd anniversary, with a notched tonneau bezel and a small gold Maltese cross set into the case flank at 5 o'clock. The 2022 Historiques reissue in yellow gold reproduced it at 37mm almost line for line, down to the flank cross, on the modern caliber 2455/2. The steel version followed in 2025 at $32,000, and vintage 222s have been repriced upward in its wake.
narrative.collector_notes: Reissue versus vintage is the whole conversation: the 4200H is a modern watch with a sapphire back and current water resistance, while original 44018 examples carry the collector premium. On the reissue, check the flank Maltese cross and bracelet taper for damage — both are expensive to make right.
